text:
Edmonton's record still says contender: 38 points, a 96% playoff chance by our simulations, a +24 goal difference. The underlying numbers have been saying something else for a while. The Oilers have only 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances on both sides) and a -1.8 expected goal difference; the rest is finishing, 25.7 goals more than their chances usually produce. Now they are winless in four (0-3-1), outscored 20-12, and the chances in that stretch were worse, 44%. This is the week the bill came due.

Some of it is who is missing. Zach Hyman is out with migraines affecting his eye, and Mike Babcock, asked about him, said: "He's on a journey trying to figure things out." Filip Hallander has an MCL sprain. Connor McDavid has moved onto the line with Kirby Dach and Kasperi Kapanen, and Kapanen is up to the top power-play unit; he is our sleeper tonight, 47% for a point with his ice time rising. McDavid can match Mark Messier's home scoring streak tonight, per Yahoo Sports. Vasily Podkolzin has eight points in a six-game streak and Tristan Jarry is the one Oiler who has been better than his chances lately: .925 over his last five starts.

Seattle is 2-3 in its last five and lost 3-1 to Chicago on Wednesday, a night Alison Lukan summed up with Lane Lambert's words, "not good enough tonight." The Kraken have been outchanced this season too (45% at five on five) and play without Jared McCann until January. Berkly Catton, whose first NHL hat trick last week set a Kraken record, is up to 16:25 a night since McCann went out. Jordan Eberle is two points from 800 in the building where his career started.

This is the first of a home-and-home. Our numbers favour Edmonton, 3.22 expected goals to 2.50, and Philipp Grubauer starts for Seattle.
headline: Oilers' luck runs dry as Kraken come to town
